description.narrative: Oour Voices Our Futures (OVOF) will use capacity-building and convenings among feminist movements to strengthen and build movements within countries and across regions, while also link feminist movements to relevant actors, such as internet rights’ movements, Dutch allies and progressive policymakers. OVOF believes in strengthening movements from within, to create more inclusive, powerful and resilient movements. To influence laws and policies at national and international levels, OVOF sees this as the only sustainable mitigation strategy in relation to the increasing power of anti-rights and anti-gender forces.

This result is reported by CREA on behalf of OVOF as it is joint activity. OVOF hosted the second ARTivism for Change event during the 69th Commission on the Status of Women (CSW). Held at the Blue Gallery in New York, this co-created community space served as a platform for creative expression and collective engagement. The event showcased how art and activism intersect to highlight and address the critical issues discussed at the CSW, offering participants innovative ways to connect with and influence global advocacy efforts. The event also served as a political platform, notably hosting the "Access Denied" campaign installation to protest the systemic visa refusals impacting Global South activists.

As a consortium, OVOF will conduct 3 regional partner convenings in 2023 and 2024 to connect the various local partners with each other to network, learn and collaborate, and will organise 2 activists convenings including exploring possibilities to expand the Changing Faces Changing Spaces Pan-African Conference to other OVOF regions.

This result is reported by CREA on behalf of OVOF as it is joint activity.1. OVOF co-supported a global delegation of sex workers at HRC59 (Human Rights Council session) in 2025 led by global sex workers alliances and allies which resulted in sex workers from OVOF countries sharing their country and regional advocacy priorities with Special Rapporteurs, making oral statements in sessions and meeting country missions. Key issues highlighted in statements during interactive dialogue were on violence against women and girls, gender-based violence in conflict, digital surveillance, sex-based framings that erase trans people, and labour rights for sex workers and domestic workers. 2. OVOF partners participated in and led teach-ins at the global feminist gathering ReCon2025.
